other.title: Synthetic MeshCompute Utility Token White Paper

sections.summary: This summary provides key information about the MeshCompute utility token. It is intended to support the prospective holder in making an informed decision. The summary covers the offeror, the project, the offer to the public, the rights and obligations attached to the token, the underlying technology, the principal risks, and the environmental impact of the consensus mechanism. The full white paper must be read alongside this summary.
sections.risk_warning: The crypto-asset described in this white paper may lose its value in part or in full, may not always be transferable, and may not be liquid. Past performance of the MeshCompute token is not indicative of future performance. The crypto-asset is not covered by an investor compensation scheme or a deposit guarantee scheme. The risk of total loss is real and the holder should not invest amounts that cannot be lost in full.
sections.management_statement: The management body of the offeror declares that this white paper complies with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCAR), that the information presented is fair, clear, and not misleading, and that no information has been omitted that would be material to the assessment of the crypto-asset. The management body assumes responsibility for the content of this white paper.
sections.notification_date: Synthetic fixture notification date placeholder for reviewer demo only.
sections.language: This white paper is drawn up in English, a language customary in the sphere of international finance, and a German-language translation is available on the offeror's project portal.
sections.offeror: MeshCompute Labs UG (haftungsbeschränkt) is a fictional synthetic offeror used only for this local fixture. The fixture legal form is an Unternehmergesellschaft (haftungsbeschränkt) organised under the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, with a fictional registered seat and business address at Example Street 22, 10115 Berlin, and a fictional commercial register reference HRB 000000.
sections.issuer: The issuer of the MeshCompute token is the same legal entity as the offeror. No separate issuer exists. The offeror holds the relevant rights to issue the token on the underlying protocol and is registered as described above.
sections.trading_platform_operator: Not applicable. The white paper is drawn up by the offeror. The token is not currently admitted to trading on a regulated trading platform operator.
sections.project: The MeshCompute project develops a decentralised marketplace for verifiable off-chain compute, with the purpose of allowing AI inference workloads to be priced and settled against verifiable execution proofs. The business model is based on protocol fees on settled compute, paid in the native token by buyers of compute capacity. The founding team consists of three engineers with prior experience in distributed systems, ZK proof systems, and high-throughput payments infrastructure.
sections.offer_or_admission: The offer is addressed to professional and eligible counterparty customers, and to retail customers in selected European Union jurisdictions for which the offeror has completed the passporting notification. The offer is conducted at a fixed subscription price denominated in euro, in two tranches, with a hard cap on the total amount offered. The target market includes developers and operators of compute-intensive AI workloads. The jurisdictions outside the scope of the passport are listed in Annex 1 to this white paper.
sections.crypto_asset: The MeshCompute token is a crypto-asset within the meaning of Art. 3(1)(5) MiCAR. The total supply is fixed at one billion units and is recorded in the smart contract documentation. The token may be transferred between addresses on the underlying protocol with no whitelist restriction. The functionality of the token is to settle protocol fees and to grant access rights to verifiable compute scheduling.
sections.rights_and_obligations: The holder has the contractual right to use the token to pay protocol fees on the MeshCompute marketplace and to enforce these rights against the offeror in accordance with the terms of service. The holder has no right to redemption against the offeror, no claim against the offeror's assets, and no equity-like rights. The obligations of the holder include compliance with applicable transfer restrictions and the offeror's terms of service.
sections.technology: The MeshCompute token is issued on the Ethereum mainnet, which uses a proof-of-stake consensus mechanism. The smart contract implementation has been audited by two independent code security firms. Custody of user funds is the responsibility of the user; no custody is provided by the offeror. The protocol is open source and the deployed contract address is published on the offeror's portal.
sections.risks: The principal risks include market risk on the token price, project risk including failure of the marketplace to attract sufficient supply or demand, technology risk including smart contract failure and protocol-level bugs, regulatory risk including future changes in MiCAR or AML/CFT requirements, liquidity risk including the absence of a deep secondary market, and operational risk including infrastructure outages. Each risk is described in detail in the dedicated risk section of this white paper, together with mitigation measures.
sections.environmental_impact: The consensus mechanism of the underlying protocol is proof-of-stake, which consumes substantially less energy than proof-of-work consensus mechanisms. The offeror monitors the energy and climate-related impact metrics for the underlying protocol as published by independent third parties and publishes the annual environmental and climate-related impact data in line with the ESMA regulatory technical standards on sustainability indicators for distributed ledger technology.

sections.summary: This summary provides key information about the EuroStable asset-referenced token (ART). It is intended to support the prospective holder in making an informed decision. The summary covers the issuer and its authorisation, the reference assets and stabilisation mechanism, the rights of holders including the redemption right at par, the principal risks, the reserve composition and segregation, the technology, and the redemption procedure. The full white paper, including the management body statement, must be read alongside this summary and is the controlling document for the offer.
sections.risk_warning: The crypto-asset described in this white paper may lose its value in part or in full, may not always be transferable, and may not be liquid. Past performance of the EuroStable ART is not indicative of future performance. The crypto-asset is not covered by an investor compensation scheme or a deposit guarantee scheme. The risk of total loss is real and the holder should not invest amounts that cannot be lost in full.
sections.management_statement: The management body of the issuer declares that this white paper complies with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCAR), that the information presented is fair, clear, and not misleading, and that no information has been omitted that would be material to the assessment of the asset-referenced token. The management body assumes responsibility for the content of this white paper.

sections.language: This white paper is drawn up in English, a language customary in the sphere of international finance, and a German-language translation is available upon request from the issuer.
sections.issuer: EuroStable AG is a fictional synthetic issuer used only for this local fixture. The legal form used in the fixture is a stock corporation (Aktiengesellschaft) organised under the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, with a fictional registered seat and business address at Example Street 80, 10115 Berlin, and a fictional register reference HRB 000000. No real BaFin authorisation is asserted; the fixture assumes an ART authorisation field remains under lawyer review. The management body consists of three fictional members with combined prior experience in regulated payment services, treasury management, and information security.
sections.art: The EuroStable ART is an asset-referenced token within the meaning of Art. 3(1)(6) MiCAR. The reference assets consist of a basket of EUR-denominated short-dated sovereign debt instruments issued by Member States of the euro area and cash deposits at credit institutions authorised in the European Union. The basket composition is fixed within a defined target band and is rebalanced on a quarterly cycle. The stabilisation mechanism operates through one-to-one issuance and redemption against the reference value, daily reconciliation of the reserve composition against the outstanding supply, and an intra-day arbitrage channel reserved for authorised participants.
sections.offer_or_admission: The offer is addressed to professional and eligible counterparty customers in selected European Union jurisdictions and excludes retail offerings in jurisdictions where the issuer has not completed the relevant passporting notification. The issuance is conducted at the reference value plus a fixed subscription fee. The target market includes regulated payment institutions, electronic money institutions, and credit institutions seeking on-chain settlement. Admission to trading on a regulated crypto-asset trading platform may follow at the discretion of the issuer.
sections.rights_and_obligations: The holder of the EuroStable ART has the following rights against the issuer: a contractual right of redemption at par at any time in accordance with Art. 39 MiCAR, a right to file complaints under the procedure described in Section 9 of this white paper, and information rights regarding the composition of the reserve. The obligations of the holder include compliance with applicable transfer restrictions, sanctions screening, and the issuer's terms of service. The redemption right may not be waived by contract and is enforceable in the courts of the Federal Republic of Germany.
sections.technology: The EuroStable ART is issued on a permissioned protocol based on a Byzantine fault tolerant consensus mechanism. Smart contract modules govern issuance, redemption, and supply control, and were audited by two independent code security firms in February 2026 and April 2026. Custody of the underlying technical keys is provided by a regulated qualified custodian in Liechtenstein, with key management based on multi-party computation and segregated cold storage. The issuer publishes a monthly attestation of the on-chain supply.
sections.risks: The principal risks attached to the EuroStable ART include the following. Market risk arises on the reserve assets and may cause the reserve value to fall below the aggregate par value of the outstanding tokens. Credit risk arises on the reserve custodian and on each reserve counterparty, including in the event of insolvency or sanctions designation. Liquidity risk arises during a redemption surge if reserve assets cannot be converted to cash at par within the contractual settlement window. De-peg risk arises if the secondary market price of the token diverges from the reference value. Operational risk arises from smart contract failure, key compromise, validator failure, and incident response shortcomings. Regulatory risk arises from changes in MiCAR Level 2 standards, EBA guidance, and BaFin supervisory practice. Reserve impairment events trigger the cure procedure described in Section 11. The redemption right may be temporarily suspended only in narrowly defined operational or regulatory emergencies and never to manage commercial outcomes.
sections.reserve_of_assets: The reserve of assets is composed of short-dated EUR-denominated sovereign debt issued by Member States of the euro area with residual maturity of less than ninety days, and of overnight cash deposits at credit institutions authorised in the European Union. This synthetic draft states that 30% of the amount referenced in euro is held as deposits with credit institutions. The composition of the reserve is fixed within a defined target band and rebalanced on a quarterly cycle. The reserve is held by a separate special-purpose vehicle and is segregated from the issuer's own balance sheet by way of a security trust structure. Custody is provided by a fictional Tier-1 European credit institution acting as qualified custodian under a tri-party custody and segregation agreement. The valuation of the reserve is performed daily at fair value by the issuer's middle office and verified weekly by the custodian. The reserve is audited monthly by an independent statutory auditor and reconciled against the outstanding token supply on a continuous basis through automated supply oracles. Any shortfall triggers the cure procedure described in Section 11 and would be routed to lawyer review for any required authority notification.
sections.environmental_impact: The consensus mechanism used by the issuance protocol is a permissioned Byzantine fault tolerant variant that does not rely on proof-of-work and does not consume energy at the level of public proof-of-work chains. The issuer monitors the energy consumption of the validator infrastructure on a continuous basis and publishes annual environmental and climate-related impact data in line with the ESMA regulatory technical standards on sustainability indicators for distributed ledger technology. Validators source electricity from the European mainland grid, with a contracted renewable share that is reported alongside the annual disclosure. The methodology, scope, and limitations of the climate-related disclosures are described in Annex 2.
sections.redemption: The redemption right is exercisable at any time at par against the holder of record. The procedure requires a KYC-verified redemption request submitted through the issuer's portal. The timing of settlement is one business day from receipt of a complete redemption request, with cut-off at 16:00 CET for same-cycle processing. Redemption is settled by EUR bank transfer to the holder's verified bank account. Redemption fees are limited to the reserve transaction costs and do not exceed twenty basis points; fees are disclosed in advance through the issuer's portal. The redemption right may be temporarily suspended only in narrowly defined operational or regulatory emergencies as described in Section 11, with the suspension reported to BaFin within twenty-four hours and to the public on the issuer's portal.

sections.summary: This summary provides key information about the PayEUR e-money token. It is intended to support the prospective holder in making an informed decision. The summary covers the issuer as an authorised electronic money institution, the par-value redemption right of the holder, the principal risks, the safeguarding of funds received against issuance, and the technology underlying the token. The full white paper must be read alongside this summary.
sections.risk_warning: The e-money token described in this white paper may lose its value in part or in full, may not always be transferable, and may not be liquid. The token is not covered by an investor compensation scheme or a deposit guarantee scheme. The risk of loss is real and the holder should not commit funds that cannot be lost in full.
sections.management_statement: The management body of PayEUR EMI GmbH declares that this white paper complies with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCAR), that the information presented is fair, clear, and not misleading, and that no information has been omitted that would be material to the assessment of the e-money token. The management body assumes responsibility for the content of this white paper.

sections.language: This white paper is drawn up in English, a language customary in the sphere of international finance, and a German-language translation is available on the issuer's portal.
sections.issuer: Synthetic PayEUR EMI GmbH is a fictional issuer used only for this local fixture. The fixture legal form is a limited liability company organised under the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, with a fictional registered seat at Example Avenue 12, 10115 Berlin, and a fictional register reference HRB 000000. No real electronic money authorisation, BaFin registration or registration number is asserted; the fixture assumes those fields remain under lawyer review for the purposes of Art. 48(1)(b) MiCAR.
sections.emt: The PayEUR is an e-money token within the meaning of Art. 3(1)(7) MiCAR. The referenced official currency is the euro. Each PayEUR unit is denominated as one euro and is issued at par against funds received in euro. The token is intended for use as a means of payment, settlement, and treasury management.
sections.offer_or_admission: The offer is addressed to professional, eligible counterparty, and retail customers in selected European Union jurisdictions for which the issuer has completed the passporting notification. The issuance is conducted at par against funds received in euro plus the applicable transaction fees. The target market includes payment institutions, merchants accepting on-chain settlement, and consumers seeking euro-denominated digital cash.
sections.rights_and_obligations: The holder has the right to redeem the e-money token at par value against the issuer at any time, with no minimum threshold, in accordance with Art. 49(4) MiCAR. The holder has no right to interest or any benefit linked to the duration of holding the token. The obligations of the holder include compliance with applicable transfer restrictions, sanctions screening, and the issuer's terms of service. The redemption right cannot be waived by contract.
sections.technology: The PayEUR is issued on a permissioned distributed ledger using a Byzantine fault tolerant consensus mechanism. Smart contract modules govern issuance, redemption, and freeze functionality. Custody of the underlying technical keys is provided by a qualified custodian under a multi-party computation key management arrangement. The issuance protocol has been audited by two independent code security firms.
sections.risks: The principal risks include market risk on the underlying euro funds, credit risk on the safeguarding credit institution, liquidity risk during a redemption surge, operational risk including smart contract failure or key compromise, redemption risk during operational emergencies, safeguarding risk should the safeguarding arrangement fail, and regulatory risk including changes in MiCAR or EMD2 Level 2 standards. Each risk is described in detail in the dedicated risk section of this white paper.
sections.environmental_impact: The consensus mechanism is a permissioned Byzantine fault tolerant variant that does not rely on proof-of-work and does not consume energy at the level of public proof-of-work chains. The issuer publishes annual environmental and climate-related impact data in line with the ESMA regulatory technical standards on sustainability indicators for distributed ledger technology. Validators are hosted on European mainland data centres.
sections.safeguarding: Funds received in exchange for issuance of the e-money token are safeguarded in accordance with Art. 7 of Directive 2009/110/EC (EMD2) as referenced by Art. 54 MiCAR. The funds are held on a segregated client money account at a Tier-1 credit institution authorised in the European Union, are not commingled with the issuer's own funds, and are protected from claims of the issuer's creditors in the event of the issuer's insolvency.
